analyticalMisses.summary: F7 was catastrophic: 0-4 for -95.00 on $95 risk. This day heavily motivates avoiding F7 as a default expression -- it carries most of a full game's variance without a full game's pricing.
Full-game moneylines went 1-4 for -89.52 -- the second-largest drag after F7.
Both four-leg parlays lost; each had winning legs but neither cleared. Small overlay positions only.

analyticalWins.summary: F5 was approximately break-even/profitable (1-1, +3.97) despite the broader card collapse -- the horizon that held up.
Team totals were also approximately break-even/profitable (1-1, +4.14).

gameLevelConcentration.note: BOS F7 lost while the BOS ML leg of the parlay won -- the horizon, not the side, was the failure.
MIL F7 and the MIL ML parlay leg both lost.
CLE ML was the day's only moneyline winner (+10.48); the parlay carrying it still lost on its other three legs.

performanceByMarketFamily.note: Catastrophic: BOS, MIL, LAD and TEX F7 all lost. The single worst family of the day and the clearest lesson.
Full-game moneylines were also poor: only CLE won; PHI, TB, MIN, CHC lost.
KC F5 won (+28.97), PIT F5 lost -- approximately break-even/profitable despite the broader card collapse.
NYY 5+ won (+24.14), CIN 4+ lost -- also approximately break-even/profitable.

processErrors.summary: Choosing F7 as a default horizon expression across four games on one card concentrated a single untested structural bet, independent of the individual sides.

proposedInvestigations.summary: Avoid F7 as a default expression; prefer F5 or full-game unless a specific, priced case for the seven-inning horizon exists (manual selection guidance only -- no production change).
Do not chase plus-money outcomes merely for payout.
Do not retune production-model math from one manual betting day.
